statement: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound. For every sufficiently large n, constructs n points in the unit square such that every triangle has area at least $`n^{-2+c}`$ for one absolute c > 0. This disproves the conjectured almost-n−2 upper bound in Heilbronn's triangle problem, which asks how large the smallest determined triangle can be.
